reading.body:
Google NBY-3 is part of a multi-county data center campus in the New Albany and Columbus region of Ohio, announced alongside $1.7 billion in combined investment across new facilities in that corridor. Google does not publish power capacity, square footage, or exact site boundaries for individual buildings within this campus, only aggregate investment figures at the state level. The facility type and scale remain undisclosed by the operator.

Within Ohio's published data center capacity, this campus ranks 9th by megawatt figure, though the state context provided does not specify which facilities compose that ranking or the total capacity attributable to the New Albany/Licking County cluster. Ohio has 76 mapped data center facilities but only 8 with published power figures totaling 60.4 MW across the entire state, meaning the vast majority of Ohio's data center footprint, including this one, operates without public capacity disclosure.

Google's presence in the New Albany corridor places it alongside AWS and Meta as a major hyperscale investor in the same region, suggesting competitive clustering around the same grid and logistics infrastructure. Without published specifications for NBY-3 itself, its material significance to AI scaling in Ohio cannot be read from disclosed facts alone, only inferred from the operator's multi-billion-dollar regional commitment and the absence of capacity data as a deliberate disclosure boundary.
